## Bounded multi-session Preview

Rei is a desktop workspace for bingo. This preview bundles platform-matching **bingo v0.6.5** from [`e036efe2e029bcbef9c191a326fafc126d935a99`](https://github.com/yexrob/bingo/commit/e036efe2e029bcbef9c191a326fafc126d935a99). The new bounded-session protocol requires this matching Core; do not substitute the v0.6.4 runtime from the previous preview.

### Changed since v0.1.0

- Keep multiple conversations alive in the same project and across projects. Switching threads does not stop other work; permissions, drafts and replies stay attached to their originating conversation.
- Large histories, tool results and room activity use bounded snapshots and incremental loading instead of flooding the renderer. Oversized recorded content can be loaded or exported through bounded transfers.
- Preserve sidebar shortcut contrast and the compact, neutral workspace presentation.
- macOS builds now use complete **ad-hoc signatures** for the app, Electron frameworks/helpers, native terminal addon and bundled bingo. Packaging verifies each native component and runs `codesign --verify --deep --strict` on the sealed app. This is **not Developer ID signing and is not notarization**.
- Packaged-runtime verification can run in a hidden, isolated temporary profile without taking desktop focus; it exercises the bundled Core and native terminal.

### Before installing

- **Preview quality; manual updates.** Verify your download against `SHA256SUMS.txt` before opening it.
- **macOS still requires per-app manual approval after downloading.** Ad-hoc signing does not establish a verified developer identity or bypass Gatekeeper. After attempting to open your verified copy of Rei, use **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** for that specific app, then confirm the macOS prompt. Only allow a copy you trust. Do not disable Gatekeeper or other system security globally. See [Apple's guidance for opening an app from an unidentified developer](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/open-a-mac-app-from-an-unknown-developer-mh40616/mac).
- Windows builds are not publisher-signed and may show security warnings. **Windows is not at full agent-tool parity:** the GUI and embedded native terminal target Windows, but bingo's agent `Bash` tool is Unix-only.
- A model provider still needs configuration. Automated tests use a local fake provider, not real cloud OAuth/accounts.
- Existing bingo configuration remains owned by bingo. Agent and room views are journal-backed; this preview has no full file explorer. Recorded file/source previews are not arbitrary live disk reads.
- Attach a project folder for work you want to keep there; the scratch workspace is temporary. The terminal runs your local shell with your user privileges.

Installers are published only after all native build and automated verification jobs succeed. These checks do not replace hands-on device testing or an independent security audit.
